_comment: Frozen D27 (54-item) instrument — single source of truth for the human-transfer analysis. Generated from site/index.html ITEMS at the time the instrument was locked. Order is canonical (resp[i] aligns to items[i]).

items.t: When someone near me is hurting, I feel it in my own chest before I've even decided to care.
Other people's troubles are their own to carry — I don't lose sleep over strangers.
My first instinct about a new person is that they probably mean well.
When someone is unusually kind to me, I quietly wonder what they're really after.
I'd rather tell you a hard truth than a comfortable lie, even when it costs me.
A small lie that spares someone's feelings is no sin at all.
The old ways earned their place; I trust what has lasted.
Tradition is mostly peer pressure from the dead — I'll decide for myself.
Rules are there for a reason, and I follow them even when no one is watching.
Authority should be questioned by default, not obeyed.
When a friend runs late and hasn't texted, I barely notice — they'll turn up.
When plans slip or people flake on me, the irritation lingers for a while.
A flaw only I would ever notice will still nag at me until it's fixed.
'Good enough' really is good enough — I finish it and move on.
Everything I own has a place, and I feel calmer when it's all in it.
My space is a cheerful mess, and I honestly don't mind.
Once I commit to something, I see it through — long after it stops being fun.
I start far more things than I ever get around to finishing.
I'll drop my plans for a good idea that lands ten minutes before it happens.
I think things through carefully before I act; I rarely leap.
If I've decided not to, I don't — temptation doesn't really move me.
Snacks, scrolling, small splurges — my willpower folds more often than I'd admit.
Harsh words sting, but an hour later I've usually set them down.
My moods can swing hard — a bright morning can curdle into a heavy afternoon.
I replay small things I said for hours, sure I got them wrong.
When something's unresolved, I can mostly let it go and sleep fine.
Small frictions — a clicking pen, someone humming — get under my skin fast.
Little annoyances slide right off me; I rarely snap.
Most days, I feel I'm roughly where I want to be in my life.
There's a low hum of 'not quite right' running under most of my days.
My face gives me away — people always seem to know what I'm feeling.
I could be coming apart inside and you'd never know it from the outside.
After a long week, the cure is a room full of people, not an empty one.
I recharge alone; too much company drains me even when I love the people.
When the plan blows up, I feel a small spark — now it gets interesting.
A sudden change of plans throws me; I need a moment to find my footing.
In a room of strangers, I somehow end up near the center of the conversation.
At a gathering I tend to hover at the edges until someone comes to me.
Making people laugh is basically how I talk.
I'm more an appreciator of humor than a performer of it.
When all the eyes in a room turn to me, something in me lights up.
Being the center of attention makes me want to quietly slip out of the room.
Steep drops, fast roads, the hottest thing on the menu — the rush is the whole point.
If it's safe and familiar, that suits me just fine.
Fitting in matters to me; I'd rather not be the odd one out.
Being seen as 'normal' has never been something I cared about.
I'm forever asking myself why I do what I do, not just what I did.
I mostly just live my life; I don't spend much time analyzing myself.
Light through a window, a well-made object — small beauty can stop me in my tracks.
I'm moved more by whether a thing works than by whether it's beautiful.
My mind naturally throws off new connections and original ideas.
I'm better at improving an existing idea than inventing one from nothing.
I love an abstract idea for its own sake, even with no use in sight.
If a discussion has no practical payoff, I lose interest fast.
